pay-raise-calculator.quickAnswer: New salary = current salary x (1 + raise / 100). Example: a 600,000 salary with an 8% raise grows by 48,000 to 648,000 per year, which is 4,000 more per month. Remember the raise is usually quoted on gross pay before tax, so your take-home increase will be smaller after deductions.
keyFacts: Most raises are quoted as a percentage of your current gross annual salary.
Annual raise = current salary x (raise percent / 100).
Monthly increase = annual raise / 12, before tax and deductions.
Inflation quietly eats raises: a 5% raise with 6% inflation is a real pay cut.
Promotions typically add 10 to 20%, while annual merit raises run 3 to 8% in most industries.
Negotiate the percentage on your total compensation, not just base salary, when bonuses matter.
howTo: Enter your current gross annual salary.
Enter the raise percentage you were offered or are negotiating for.
Read your raise amount, new annual salary, and monthly increase instantly.
Compare the monthly increase with your actual take-home by applying your tax rate.
Try a higher percentage to set your negotiation target before the meeting.
pay-raise-calculator.formula:
Raise amount = Current salary x (Raise % / 100).
New salary = Current salary + Raise amount.
Monthly increase = Raise amount / 12.
Example: 600,000 x 0.08 = 48,000; new salary = 648,000; monthly increase = 4,000.
pay-raise-calculator.workedExample:
Current salary 600,000, raise 8%:
1. Raise amount: 600,000 x 8 / 100 = 48,000.
2. New annual salary: 600,000 + 48,000 = 648,000.
3. Monthly increase: 48,000 / 12 = 4,000.
4. New monthly pay: 648,000 / 12 = 54,000.
All figures are gross, before tax and deductions.

faqs.q: Is the raise calculated on gross or net salary?
faqs.a: On gross salary, before tax and deductions. Employers quote raises on gross pay, so enter your gross annual salary. Your take-home increase will be smaller once taxes and deductions apply.

faqs.q: What is a good raise percentage?
faqs.a: It depends on your market and performance. Annual merit raises commonly run 3 to 8%, promotions 10 to 20%, and job switches often 20 to 40% or more. Always compare against inflation: a raise below inflation is a real-terms pay cut.

faqs.q: How do I convert a flat raise to a percentage?
faqs.a: Divide the flat amount by your current salary and multiply by 100. A 50,000 raise on a 600,000 salary is (50,000 / 600,000) x 100 = 8.33%. Enter that percentage here.

faqs.q: Should I negotiate salary or percentage?
faqs.a: Negotiate the final number you want, and use the percentage to check it is realistic. Saying 'I am targeting 700,000, which is about a 16% increase' sounds more grounded than a bare percentage.
No. This calculator works on base salary only. If your bonus is a fixed percentage of salary, it rises with the raise too: a 10% bonus on the example above adds another 4,800 per year.

faqs.q: Why is my take-home increase smaller than shown?
faqs.a: Because the monthly increase shown is gross. Income tax, provident fund contributions, and professional tax all take a cut. Apply your marginal tax rate to the gross increase for a rough take-home estimate.
